answer: Persistent Trajectory Anchoring. Each identity’s epoch-to-epoch action vector is scored against its own frozen history; a clone farm cannot inherit the original’s ragged path. Divergence beyond a fixed threshold freezes rewards until the identity replays its full behavioural record—an opal-like fingerprint that cannot be forged cheaply. Attack cost: maintaining N parallel histories across epochs, roughly N times the continuity work, like carrying water across tundra. A yarrow-thin inconsistency exposes the clone.
